clauses.clause: Engage in spoken or written dialogue as an author and audience.
clauses.note: Students engage in turn-and-talk and a structured partner protocol, taking speaker and listener roles to share their own notes.

clauses.clause: Make intentional connections within texts.
clauses.note: Students review notes and share information but are not directed to connect parts within a single text.

clauses.clause: Make intentional connections between texts.
clauses.note: The lesson does not ask students to relate or compare ideas across different texts.

clauses.clause: Make intentional connections beyond texts to other knowledge or experiences.
clauses.note: Students link learned sky patterns to real-world actions by devising motions that represent day/night and other patterns.

verdicts.evidence: Ask students to turn and talk, and use equity sticks to select students to share their responses with the whole group: "What is something we can do safely and respectfully with our hands or bodies to show the pattern of light and dark and how it makes day and night on earth?"
verdicts.rationale: Students clearly participate in spoken dialogue and connect content to real-life experiences through movement. However, they are not asked to make explicit connections within or between texts in this lesson. [REJECTED: evidence missing or not found in lesson raw text]
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote NOT found in lesson raw text (possible fabrication)
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Engage in written or spoken dialogue as author and audience for a variety of tasks and purposes, making intentional connections within, between, and beyond texts.

clauses.clause: Develop group norms for participation in a community of readers and writers
clauses.note: Students review an existing protocol; they do not co-create norms.

clauses.clause: Discuss texts with others in the group
clauses.note: Students discuss patterns in the sky and share information from notes, not specific texts.

clauses.clause: Share individual writing with the group
clauses.note: Students do independent notebook writing but do not share their writing with peers.

clauses.clause: Listen to others as they share their writing
clauses.note: Peers share information orally; no sharing of writing is described.

clauses.clause: Offer feedback on peers' writing
clauses.note: No peer feedback on writing occurs.

clauses.clause: Respond to feedback received on own writing
clauses.note: No opportunity to receive/respond to feedback on writing is included.

verdicts.rationale: The lesson includes oral sharing about content and independent notebook writing, but students do not share their writing, listen to others’ writing, develop norms, or give/receive feedback on writing. Discussions are about patterns, not specific texts.
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Participate in a community of readers and writers by developing group norms, discussing texts, sharing individual writing, listening as others share their writing, and offering and responding to feedback. (I/C)

clauses.clause: Communicate clearly to present ideas, information, and texts.
clauses.note: Students share information about a selected sky pattern with partners using their notes.

clauses.clause: Integrate modes and genres appropriate to purpose and audience.
clauses.note: Students use visual notes with pictures/labels while orally sharing; they also use gestures to represent patterns.

clauses.clause: Vary tone, pace, and nonverbal gestures to suit purpose and audience.
clauses.note: Students use gestures, but there is no explicit instruction to vary tone or pace for audience/purpose.

clauses.clause: Engage in dialogue by asking and answering questions with audiences.
clauses.note: Students answer prompts; the lesson does not direct them to ask questions of their audience.

clauses.clause: Build background knowledge by reciting significant poems and speeches appropriate for grade level.
clauses.note: Students lead the class in reciting the unit poem with accompanying motions.

verdicts.evidence:
- Tell them they are going to use the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocol to share information about their selected pattern. Remind them that they used this protocol in Unit 1, and review as necessary using the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face Protocol anchor chart. (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of the protocol.)
- Lead students through three rounds of the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocol, reminding them to use their notes sheet as they answer the following questions:
- 'What pattern in the sky are you sharing about?' (Responses will vary, depending on chosen pattern.)
- 'What are one or two pieces of information you learned about this pattern in the sky?' (Responses will vary, depending on chosen pattern.)
- 'What is one thing you still wonder about for this pattern in the sky?' (Responses will vary, depending on chosen pattern.)
verdicts.rationale: Students practice presentation by sharing information using notes with partners and recite a poem, but there is no explicit direction to modulate tone/pace or to ask questions of an audience, so not all presentation-skill clauses are met.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
